title: The whole-litre rounding gap
hook: 250mL per cup can leave a whole-litre fill above the exact requirement.

knows: that a model can declare hypothetical quantities
doesNotKnow: Compute excess created by rounding a volume to coarse increments.

misconception: A rounded fill volume always equals the exact serving volume.
objective: Compute excess created by rounding a volume to coarse increments.

claims.text: Each empty cup is allocated 250mL. Compare exact total volume with that total rounded up to whole litres. Scaled model; empty cups; volume only; no heating guidance.
claims.source: Declared hypothetical inputs and limits in resource-specs.json. No actual product, price, tariff, shelf-life, treatment or physical appliance specification is asserted. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: The stage's two results are computed by the printed expressions. At Cups=5, A=1.25L and B=2L. Geometry follows the declared dimension relationships. Other pictures use a fixed full scale across the slider range; continuous fills and arcs show relative amounts rather than literal object counts.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["/",["*","x",250],1000]; B=["ceil",["/",["*","x",250],1000]]; x denotes Cups. At x=5, A=1.25, B=2. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals. Diagram scale: resourceGraphicScale in resource-model.ts takes the maximum modeled magnitude across both formulas and the declared slider range. For non-geometry figures, full-scale values are displayed; the scale stays fixed when the slider changes. Energy axis endpoints use resourceAxisEnd, including B=5×A hours in lh-watts-hours-trade; cylinder rx and ry both scale with radius in resourceCylinderDimensions. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: Multiply cup count by millilitres per cup, then convert to litres. Rounding up introduces an excess that is visible as the difference between the two results. Exact need and a coarse fill increment are different quantities.

recall.question: Each cup is allocated 250mL and the fill is rounded up to whole litres. For nine cups, how much is the excess over the exact need?
recall.why: Exact need is 9 × 250mL = 2.25L; rounding up gives 3L, an excess of 0.75L.
